title: Support for you. Understanding for your teenager.
standfirst: Parenting a teenager can leave you carrying questions you never expected. Explore practical guidance, space for yourself and a clearer route into support.

sections.heading: You do not have to arrive with the answer
paragraphs: Perhaps everyday conversations have become difficult. Perhaps school, emotions or family relationships are taking up more of your thoughts than you can comfortably manage. You may want help with a particular situation, or simply somewhere to begin.

This part of my counselling website brings my parenting work together in one place. You can understand the different ways I work, get to know Parentology and choose what feels relevant to your family.

sections.heading: Start with what you need
paragraphs: Support for you: explore parent coaching, counselling and focused conversations about your family.
Ongoing guidance: discover In-Touch, my messaging-led parent support, and see how it works.
Understanding and tools: explore RESET, my books, learning resources and workshops. If you are looking for therapy for your teenager, there is a separate young-person counselling pathway.

sections.heading: One person behind both parts of the work
paragraphs: I am Laura Thomas, a psychotherapist, parenting coach and author. Parentology is the part of my work focused on supporting parents through the teenage years. Bringing it into this website makes the relationship between parenting support and counselling easier to understand, while keeping their different purposes clear.

sections.heading: Get to know my approach
paragraphs: Watch my introduction, read about RESET or explore my two parenting books. You can start with information before deciding whether you would like to talk.
Parentology World remains a connected part of my work, including its existing workshop and resource-access journeys. Where a next step opens that website, it will be clearly labelled.

title: Find the support that fits your family
standfirst: Sometimes you need help with what is happening at home. Sometimes you need room to understand what it is bringing up for you. We can start by working out which support fits.

sections.heading: Different needs deserve a clear choice
paragraphs: Parenting support does not have to mean choosing the same kind of help for everyone. This page explains the options so you can understand what each is for before making an enquiry.

sections.heading: Practical parent coaching
paragraphs: Coaching focuses on situations you want to think through: communication, conflict, school difficulties or uncertainty about how to respond. The conversation centres on understanding your family context and considering practical ways forward.
If you want continuing contact around everyday situations, read about In-Touch. If you want a focused planning conversation, ask about the current strategy-session options.

sections.heading: Counselling for you
paragraphs: You may be feeling stretched, worried or caught between your own needs and those of your family. Counselling offers space to explore your experience, rather than focusing only on a parenting strategy.
The counselling section explains the way I work and the services available. Couples and family support have their own pages, so you can consider them in the right context.

sections.heading: Support for your teenager
paragraphs: Looking for help as a parent is different from arranging counselling for a young person. My young-person counselling page explains that separate route. We can discuss which kind of enquiry you are making without treating the two as interchangeable.

sections.heading: An enquiry is a place to begin
paragraphs: Tell me briefly what you would like help with. You do not need to send your family’s full story through a website form. We can discuss the next step and the practical arrangements before you decide.

meta_description: Compare parent coaching, counselling and ongoing guidance with Laura Thomas, and find a suitable route into support for you or your family.

title: A continuing connection through In-Touch
standfirst: In-Touch is my messaging-led support for parents who want a continuing conversation about the situations arising in family life.

sections.heading: When another question comes up
paragraphs: A difficult conversation does not always happen just before an appointment. You might want to reflect on what happened, think through a response or return to something we have already discussed. In-Touch is designed around that need for continuing parent guidance.

sections.heading: Understand the arrangement before you begin
paragraphs: We start by discussing your family situation and whether this way of working is suitable. The agreed arrangement sets out how contact works, what is included and when replies are available.
Voice or text messages provide a way to bring a situation into the conversation. Guidance relates to the context you share; this is a relationship with a practitioner, not an automated advice tool.

sections.heading: Clear boundaries matter
paragraphs: In-Touch is not an emergency or continuously monitored service. Working days, response windows and any session allowance need to be agreed before support begins. There is no promise of an immediate reply.
If your main need is your own therapeutic space or counselling for a young person, those services have separate explanations and enquiry routes.

sections.heading: How this connects to the wider work
paragraphs: You may come across ideas from RESET, a relevant resource or one of my books. They support the conversation rather than replacing an understanding of your particular circumstances.

sections.heading: Find out whether it fits
paragraphs: An introductory conversation can cover your questions, the current format and the practical terms. Current options will be explained before you commit. If In-Touch is not suitable, we can discuss a more relevant next step.

title: A more considered response, with RESET
standfirst: RESET is the framework I use to organise a more thoughtful response when family interactions feel difficult. Here is an introduction to its purpose and the ideas behind it.

sections.heading: A structure for the conversation
paragraphs: When there is a lot happening at once, it can be hard to decide what deserves your attention. RESET brings together noticing the situation, understanding emotion, communicating what matters and considering a next step. It is an approach to explore in context, rather than a script that fits every family.

sections.heading: Recognise the issue
paragraphs: Begin by considering what may be happening in the situation, rather than relying only on the behaviour you first notice.

sections.heading: Empathise in the moment
paragraphs: The framework makes room for the teenager’s perspective and the experience behind the interaction.

sections.heading: Say what matters
paragraphs: Consider the important message, value or boundary, and how it can be expressed clearly.

sections.heading: Emotionally regulate together
paragraphs: This part of the approach focuses on emotional steadiness within the interaction.

sections.heading: Take action with confidence
paragraphs: The final step concerns a considered response to the situation, informed by what came before.

sections.heading: Explore it with the right context
paragraphs: The framework does not replace individual assessment or professional support when that is needed. My parenting services, resources and books offer ways to explore related ideas in context.

title: Something useful for the moment you are in
standfirst: You may want something to read, a conversation to watch or a resource to return to later. Start with the question on your mind, then choose a format that suits you.

sections.heading: Find your starting point
paragraphs: Browse resources around communication, emotional overwhelm, confidence, school experiences and the teenage years. These groupings help you find relevant material without needing to know the name of a particular guide.

sections.heading: Read
paragraphs: Explore Parenting Unstoppable Girls and Parenting Teen Boys with Confidence, alongside approved guides, journals and conversation prompts. Each resource card explains what it is, who it is for and how to access it.
Book pages bring the publication information and related support together. Topic links reflect relevant themes; they do not claim to reproduce a chapter or replace reading the book.

sections.heading: Watch
paragraphs: Video cards introduce a recording before you load the player. You can see the subject and any access requirement, then choose whether to watch. Where available, an approved text summary or captions provide another way to follow the material.

sections.heading: Learn in your own time
paragraphs: The workshop collection explains the available recordings and supporting materials. Paid workshops are labelled clearly, with details available before you reach the existing purchase page.

sections.heading: Know what happens next
paragraphs: Some resources may be freely available; others may require sign-up, membership or purchase. The label beside each item explains this before you leave the page. Material hosted on Parentology World opens through its existing authorised access route.

sections.heading: When a resource is not enough
paragraphs: If you would rather discuss what is happening in your own family, explore parent support or make an enquiry. You can return to the tools alongside suitable support, rather than having to work everything out from a download.

title: Make room to understand, in your own time
standfirst: A workshop can give you a focused introduction to a subject you want to understand better, with space to watch and reflect at a time that works for you.

sections.heading: Choose the subject that matters now
paragraphs: When parenting feels too much: discover the Parent Overwhelm Reset, a recorded workshop with accompanying material.
Understanding self-harm: explore an educational awareness workshop for parents, with a supporting toolkit. Each workshop has a separate information page explaining its scope and access.

sections.heading: See the detail before you decide
paragraphs: Workshop cards identify the subject, format and access type. Open a detail page to understand the intended audience and included materials before continuing to a purchase or access destination.
A paid workshop is different from a free replay or a commissioned talk. Those formats are labelled separately so you can choose deliberately.

sections.heading: Learning connected to Laura’s work
paragraphs: These workshops sit alongside my parenting support, RESET introduction and published books. They provide educational material; they do not establish a counselling relationship or provide an individual assessment.

sections.heading: Access through Parentology
paragraphs: Where an existing Parentology product supplies the recording and materials, purchase and access continue through that service. The link will tell you when you are leaving the counselling website. Current terms and product information should be checked before purchase.

sections.heading: Looking for something for a group?
paragraphs: Schools and parent groups can enquire about a talk or workshop. That is a separate conversation about audience, subject and format, rather than a place in an on-demand product.

title: When parenting feels too much
standfirst: An introduction to the Parent Overwhelm Reset: a recorded workshop for parents who want to make space to consider their own experience of overwhelm.

sections.heading: When your own experience needs attention
paragraphs: Parenting can involve holding many things in mind at once. This workshop turns attention towards the parent, offering a focused place to engage with Laura’s educational material away from the pace of everyday interactions.

sections.heading: What you are choosing
paragraphs: The existing Parent Overwhelm Reset brings together a recorded presentation and an accompanying guide. This page helps you understand the format before you open the Parentology product page.
It is a self-paced learning resource. It does not include an individual assessment, a personal response to your circumstances or ongoing contact unless separately agreed through a service.

sections.heading: A place within the wider picture
paragraphs: You can explore the RESET introduction and related parenting resources here. If you want to talk about your own situation, parent coaching and counselling have separate explanations so you can compare the options.

sections.heading: Check the current product details
paragraphs: Before purchase, check the confirmed materials, price, access arrangements and terms on the existing Parentology product page. Purchasing and delivery stay within that established system.
You will be told clearly that the next link opens Parentology World. No payment or account details are collected on this information page.

title: Understanding self-harm: a workshop for parents
standfirst: An educational workshop for parents who want to understand the subject of self-harm and the scope of the support material Laura has created.

sections.heading: Understand the scope first
paragraphs: This is the existing Self-Harm and Suicide Awareness Workshop. The purpose of this page is to explain the resource clearly and help you decide whether to read its full product information. It is not a screening tool or a personal assessment.

sections.heading: The workshop and toolkit
paragraphs: The existing product brings together workshop material and a printable supporting toolkit. Read the product information to understand the recording, included files and access arrangements before making a purchase.

sections.heading: Education and individual support have different roles
paragraphs: A recording cannot assess a young person’s circumstances or provide an emergency response. Viewing or purchasing it does not arrange clinical care. If your enquiry is about counselling for a young person or support for you as a parent, use the relevant service page to understand that separate route.

sections.heading: Explore before purchasing
paragraphs: The workshop is supplied through the existing Parentology product journey. The next link opens that website, where you can check current product details and terms. There is no new checkout or member area on this page.

sections.heading: A careful connection to further reading
paragraphs: Related books, parent guidance and suitable resources can sit alongside this workshop once their relevance has been checked. They should be presented as further information, without promises of prevention or an outcome for an individual family.

sections.heading: Make the question specific
paragraphs: Is it finding a way to begin a conversation, expressing an important boundary or deciding what needs a fuller discussion? Laura’s approved explanation will address these different needs rather than offering one script for every interaction.

sections.heading: Connect the ideas
